records.title: Catalytic and fluid catalytic cracking for refinery/fuel performance
records.sourceNativeSummary: Catalytic cracking improved conversion of heavy petroleum into higher-octane fuels; fluid catalytic cracking then coupled reaction and catalyst regeneration through circulating fluidized solids, reaching commercial operation under wartime fuel pressure.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Wartime aviation-fuel demand accelerated scale but does not mean every refinery objective favored FCC; feedstock, product slate, catalyst life and plant complexity remain conditional.

sources.supports: three-year concept-to-commercial FCC development and fluid-solids scale
WWII pressure, commercial-scale reactor and FCC innovation history

records.title: Fischer–Tropsch synthetic fuels under resource/strategic constraints
records.sourceNativeSummary: Fischer–Tropsch converted synthesis gas into liquid hydrocarbons and was industrialized in Germany where coal availability and oil constraints changed the economic/strategic value of synthetic fuel.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A technically feasible fuel route can be globally uneconomic yet locally valuable under resource/geopolitical constraints; wartime use does not imply peacetime cost or environmental superiority.

sources.supports: Fischer–Tropsch refinery history and process configuration
historical synthetic petroleum and German 1926–45 lineage references

records.title: Richardson hand-computed numerical weather prediction
records.sourceNativeSummary: Richardson formulated atmospheric prediction as numerical integration of physical equations and hand-computed a six-hour pressure change during/after WWI-era work, but the calculation took weeks and produced an unrealistic result.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The formulation could be scientifically productive while operationally unusable: compute speed, initial observations, numerical balance/filtering and error structure were missing complements. Correct equations do not imply current tractability.

sources.supports: 1922 numerical weather prediction and pre-computer computational burden
six-week hand calculation, unrealistic result and 64,000-computer forecast-factory concept

records.title: Rigid passenger airships from successful service to route collapse
records.sourceNativeSummary: Rigid airships achieved real long-distance passenger service and demonstrated range/endurance advantages, but the Hindenburg disaster, operating/weather risk and improving heavier-than-air aircraft destroyed the route’s commercial/safety position.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A route can be technically successful for years yet lose when the broader risk/economic frontier changes; one famous accident should not be mistaken for the sole causal explanation.

records.title: Lysenkoist agricultural genetics as institutionally amplified invalid science
records.sourceNativeSummary: Lysenkoism gained Soviet institutional authority while suppressing Mendelian/genetic competitors and marginalizing or persecuting geneticists. Political endorsement changed which claims could be researched or criticized without making the claims biologically true.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Institutional adoption and policy reach are not validation. Conversely, later rejection of Lysenkoism should not erase the need to explain why its agronomic promises and political fit appeared attractive under contemporary pressures.

sources.supports: Muller’s opposition to politicized Lysenkoism and resulting marginalization in the USSR

records.title: Whittle–von Ohain independent turbojet-development routes
records.sourceNativeSummary: British Frank Whittle and German Hans von Ohain independently developed turbojet engines during the 1930s. Germany achieved a turbojet-powered flight in 1939 and Britain in 1941; wartime transfer then accelerated U.S. work.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Independent convergence does not imply identical architectures or institutions, and first flight did not equal production-ready propulsion: compressor, materials, combustion, reliability and aircraft integration remained frontiers.

sources.supports: independent Whittle/von Ohain routes and first flights
British design transfer to U.S. and early performance shortfalls

records.title: Farnsworth–Zworykin electronic-television routes under patent/industrial competition
records.sourceNativeSummary: Mechanical television worked but had severe resolution/quality limits. Farnsworth and Zworykin pursued electronic image pickup/display routes that converged toward practical all-electronic television while RCA’s industrial/patent position shaped diffusion.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Priority and commercial dominance do not reduce the trajectory to one inventor. Electronic superiority emerged from cameras, display tubes, scanning/synchronization, transmitters and manufacturing rather than one patent.

sources.supports: mechanical television, Farnsworth/Zworykin electronic components and 1939 RCA public introduction
Farnsworth archival material and parallel inventor context
